info.name: TalkToMyChild API (Cartesia + Memory)
info.description:
Test collection for the upgraded backend.

What changed from the RunPod version:
- TTS + cloning use Cartesia. No ngrok / PUBLIC_BASE_URL.
- Characters are cloned ONCE at creation; voice_id stored on them.
- Test TTS takes an optional `voice_id` (not a voice_sample_path).
- New: 11b Call Turn (STREAM) — live STT->LLM->TTS streaming.
- New: 14 Call End — summarises the conversation into the character's rolling memory.

Set the `baseUrl` collection variable and run top-to-bottom. `character_id` and `voice_id` are auto-saved after Create Character.

request.description: Verifies GROQ_API_KEY and CARTESIA_API_KEY are set. `cloning_enabled` should be true once CARTESIA_API_KEY is present.

formdata.description: Any short clip with clear speech (mp3/wav/webm/m4a).

request.description: Cartesia TTS with the preset fallback voice (CARTESIA_FALLBACK_VOICE_ID). Response is WAV — Save Response -> Save to a file to play it. No cloning needed.
Voice cloning. Uses the {{voice_id}} auto-saved by Create Character (step 6). Returns WAV in the cloned voice. No ngrok needed — Cartesia references the voice by id.
All characters for the demo user.

formdata.description: REQUIRED: audio with ~5-20s of clear speech. Cloned via Cartesia on upload.

request.description: Creates a character and clones the uploaded voice via Cartesia. On success: 201 with character JSON including `voice_id`. Both character_id and voice_id are auto-saved to collection variables.
Details for the saved character_id. Note `voice_id` and `has_memory` fields.
Preview line in the character's voice (uses its stored voice_id; falls back to preset if cloning failed). Returns WAV.
Clears in-memory conversation history. Long-term memory (from Call End) is NOT cleared — it persists on the character.
Opening line. Body = WAV. Header X-Reply-Text holds the spoken text (URL-encoded).

formdata.description: Audio of what the kid said. 1-30s.

request.description: Full round trip, NON-streaming (easiest to test in Postman). STT->LLM->TTS. Body = WAV reply. Headers X-User-Text, X-Reply-Text (URL-encoded).

TEXT-ONLY turn for a character — no audio in, no audio out. Returns {"user_text": "...", "reply": "..."}. Shares the same in-memory history as '11. Call Turn' and '11b. Call Turn (STREAM)', so this can be mixed with audio-based turns in the same session. This is what the call screen's 'Type instead' toggle uses.

TEXT-ONLY chat with NO character (the 'Quick Chat' page). Stateless on the server — the client sends the running conversation back each turn in `history` ([{"role":"user"|"assistant","content":"..."}]). Returns {"reply": "..."}. Uses the same persona as `python voice_agent.py --generic`, so it matches the generic voice call.

formdata.description: Audio of what the kid said.

request.description:
LIVE turn. STT -> streaming LLM -> streaming TTS, sentence by sentence.

Response body is RAW PCM (s16le), streamed as it's generated — NOT a playable WAV file on its own. Postman can't play raw PCM directly; this endpoint is meant for the frontend client to play through the Web Audio API.

Headers:
  X-User-Text  — what STT heard (URL-encoded)
  X-Sample-Rate — PCM sample rate (e.g. 44100)

To verify in Postman, just confirm you get a 200 with a large binary body and the X-User-Text header. Get the final reply text via Call History (step 12) after.
Conversation so far (in-memory, current server process).

Ends the session: summarises the conversation into the character's rolling long-term memory, then clears in-memory history.

Returns {"ok": true, "memory": "..."}. Run Get Character (step 7) afterwards and you'll see has_memory = true. Start a new call (steps 9-11) and the character will remember.
Deletes the character and its local files (image + voice sample). Note: the Cartesia clone itself is not deleted by this — remove it in the Cartesia dashboard if needed.
